messages:
alex: Quick follow-up to the RFC about the hosting/dedicated/private abstraction — I want to propose a "slimline" interface we can rely on long-term. Key ideas: capability discovery + a tiny probe endpoint + an explicit small config translation layer. Thoughts?

maria: +1 to capability discovery. Do we still want sidecar creds pinned to the adapter or handed via control plane on every probe?

dan: prefer control-plane-signed shortlived creds. Sidecar pinned creds cause churn when we rotate. Also think through KV cache eviction semantics across hosted vs private: prefix caches vs tenant-isolated caches behave differently.

jamie: Sketch of capability manifest I'm imagining:
```json
{
  "capabilities": ["kv_cache","streaming","batching_profiles"],
  "version": "1.1",
  "probe_endpoint": "/internal/adapter/probe"
}
```
Jamie's note: probe should return supported sequence lengths, max batch size, and a small perf profile.

ops-bot: added to #architecture agenda for tomorrow's sync :calendar: (auto-note)

eric: Warning: if we make capability negotiation mandatory at request time, private (air-gapped) customers that disable egress for control plane calls will break the happy path. We should allow a cached manifest mode with TTL and a explicit "offline" fallback policy list, e.g. `manifest -> local-variant -> dedicated -> hosted` (last two only if allowed by tenant policy).

maria: Also: telemetry mapping concern — we need a canonical mapping from adapter metrics to console dashboards for per-tenant unit economics. If adapters report slightly different names we lose cost attribution. Propose a small telemetry shim that maps to: `route, model_variant, batching_profile, tenant_id`.

jamie: Agree on telemetry. Proposed unified schema snippet:
```yaml
telemetry:
  labels: [route, model_variant, batching_profile, tenant_id]
  metrics: [tokens_generated, requests_count, tail_latency_ms]
```
This keeps the console side simple and deterministic.

dan: I can prototype a minimal shim (translate adapter manifest + telemetry) by EOW. Quick question: do we want the probe to return a machine-readable fallback policy? or keep that logic in control plane? :thinking:

alex: Keep probe minimal: capability manifest + perf hints + TTL for offline mode. Fallback policy decisions should live in control plane so we can A/B test routing without touching adapters. I'll file a follow-up RFC with the proposed shape and a small test matrix (probe behavior, manifest TTL, offline mode). @ops-bot can you add the RFC to next sprint board? :thumbsup:

sre-bot: NOTE: when you draft the RFC, include failure modes: stale manifest, manifest downgrade, and mixed-capability routing. Those are where we'll see incidents.

alex: Good call — will include incident scenarios and a canary rollout plan. Thanks everyone.
